protocol.name: treeland_output_group_manager_unstable_v1
protocol.copyright: SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2024 - 2026 UnionTech Software Technology Co., Ltd. SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
protocol.description:
This protocol lets a privileged client such as the DDE display settings panel organize physical outputs into mirroring groups: one source output whose rendered content is duplicated to one or more mirror outputs, so that several screens show the same desktop. This is the "copy mode" of the compositor, as opposed to the default "extension" mode where each output shows an independent desktop region.
The protocol exposes a singleton manager global that creates and tracks treeland_output_group_v1 objects. Each group designates a single source output and an ordered list of mirror outputs, all addressed by opaque uuid strings. While copy mode is engaged the compositor exposes a wl_output only for the source output; mirror uuids come from treeland-output-uuid-head-unstable-v1 instead (see treeland_output_group_v1 for details). An output may belong to at most one group at a time, and a group drives copy mode only while it has both a source and at least one mirror.
The compositor persists the set of groups and their configuration (name, configured source uuid, and configured mirror uuid list) across compositor restarts and restores them on startup, so groups survive reboots and reappear as group_added events on bind; this lets a privileged client configure mirroring once and have it reapply automatically later. An output must be connected and enabled when it is first added to a group (via create_group, set_source, or add_output); once configured it is kept across unplug/replug and compositor restart and auto-resumes when the output returns. The name never changes; the configured source and mirror list persist until a client changes them with set_source, add_output, remove_output, or dissolve.
The terms "must", "must not", "should", and "may" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.
Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development. It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways, without incrementing the interface major version and without prior notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or semantics remaining stable across releases.

interface.name: treeland_output_group_manager_v1
interface.description:
A singleton global that creates treeland_output_group_v1 objects and broadcasts the set of existing groups to bound clients.
On bind the compositor emits one group_added event carrying the name of each existing group, followed by a single groups_done event, so the client can distinguish the initial dump of pre-existing groups from later group_added events for groups created after the bind. When any client creates a group every other bound client receives group_added for it, and when a group is dissolved every bound client receives group_removed. Clients therefore never poll for the group set; they obtain a group object for a name with the get_group request when they need to observe or edit that group.
Multiple privileged clients such as the DDE display settings panel may bind and use the protocol concurrently. Commits from all clients are applied in arrival order; an output claimed by one group is rejected for another with the non-fatal output_in_use failure, so concurrent edits never terminate a connection and clients may retry or adjust.

request.name: destroy
request.description:
Destroy the treeland_output_group_manager_v1 object and release the client's binding to the manager global.
Existing treeland_output_group_v1 objects are not affected and remain valid until they are destroyed or the compositor dissolves the group. The client must destroy each group object separately; the compositor does not cascade destruction from the manager.

request.name: create_group
request.description:
Create a new treeland_output_group_v1 object with the given initial source output. An empty source creates a group with no source; the client adds mirrors afterwards with add_output and may change the source with set_source, then commits to apply the changes. Copy mode engages once the group has both a source and at least one mirror after commit.
The compositor assigns a unique name to the new group; names are chosen by the compositor, not by clients. The client learns the name from the name event, which the compositor emits on the new group object before any other event. The name identifies the group in the manager's group_removed event.
If the source cannot be applied — a non-empty source that does not identify a connected enabled output, or one that is already a member of another group — the group is still created with an empty source: the initial state event reports an empty source uuid, and the compositor emits an operation_failed event on the new group object before its done event, with invalid_output when the uuid does not identify a connected enabled output or output_in_use when it is already claimed by another group. The client may later set a source with set_source or add mirrors with add_output, then commit to apply them.
On success the compositor broadcasts a group_added event carrying the new group's name to every other bound client; the caller learns the name from the name event on its new group object and does not get a group_added event for it. Other clients obtain a group object for that name with get_group.

arg.name: source
arg.summary: uuid of the initial source output, or empty for no source

request.name: get_group

description.summary: get a group object by name

request.description:
Create a new treeland_output_group_v1 object bound to the existing group with the given name, for example a group created by another client or one whose object the client has since destroyed. On success the compositor sends the initial state of the group on the new object: one name event, one state event carrying the effective source and the full mirror list in list order, then one done event marking the end of the initial batch.
The name is the compositor-assigned name reported by the name event on group objects. If the name is empty, or does not identify an existing group at the time the request is processed — for example because the group was dissolved between the group_removed event and this request — the object is still created, but it is an invalid group object: the compositor sends no name event and no state event, emits an operation_failed event with invalid_name before the done event, and afterwards rejects every request except destroy with operation_failed invalid_name. The client should destroy the object.
On success the returned object is an independent handle: destroying it does not dissolve the group, and several clients may hold objects bound to the same group at the same time.

arg.name: id
arg.summary: a new group object bound to the named group

arg.name: name
arg.summary: the compositor-assigned name of the group

event.name: group_added
event.description:
Emitted when an output group is created by any client. Each bound client receives this event once per existing group on bind, and again whenever a new group is created — except for the client that created the group, which learns the name from the name event on its create_group return object instead.
The name argument is the compositor-assigned name of the new group. A client that wants to observe or edit the group obtains a group object with the manager's get_group request.

arg.name: name
arg.summary: the compositor-assigned name of the new group

event.name: groups_done
event.description: Emitted exactly once, after the compositor has finished sending the bind-time group_added events for all groups that existed when the client bound. A client receiving this event knows it has seen the complete initial set and that any later group_added is for a group created after the bind.

event.name: group_removed
event.description: Emitted when an output group is dissolved, whether because a client sent the dissolve request or because the compositor removed it as a whole. Every bound client receives this event for the group; any group objects that client holds for it receive a removed event and must be destroyed afterwards.

arg.name: name
arg.summary: the name of the dissolved group

interface.name: treeland_output_group_v1
interface.description:
Represents one mirroring group: a source output, identified by its uuid, whose content is duplicated to an ordered list of mirror outputs, each identified by its uuid. Output uuids are never empty; an empty uuid in events represents the absence of a source.
While the group has both a source and at least one mirror, the compositor exposes a wl_output global only for the source output. Mirror outputs have no wl_output while copy mode is engaged, so clients cannot use wl_output-based protocols (including treeland-output-uuid-unstable-v1, which requires a wl_output) to identify them; they must instead obtain mirror uuids from the treeland-output-uuid-head-unstable-v1 protocol, which resolves a zwlr_output_head_v1 to the same uuid. A configured mirror only loses its wl_output while copy mode is actually engaged; while the group is inert (no effective source or no effective mirrors) the mirror retains its wl_output and behaves as a normal extension output. When copy mode exits — the last mirror is removed, the effective source becomes empty, or the group is dissolved — the affected outputs become normal extension outputs again and their wl_output globals come back.
The group keeps a configured source (zero or one) and a configured mirror list (zero or more). set_source, add_output, and remove_output queue changes that take effect only when the client sends commit. The state event reports the effective runtime state, not the configured state: a configured source or mirror whose output is currently unplugged or disabled is absent from that event but remains in the persisted configuration, so copy mode auto-resumes when the output comes back. An output may belong to at most one group at a time; one already in another group fails with the output_in_use failure.
Pending set_source, add_output, and remove_output requests that cannot be applied because of transient output state (e.g. an output unplugged between the request and the commit) are reported via a non-fatal operation_failed event when the commit is processed; the group is otherwise unchanged and the client may retry. Only already_dissolved — sending any request other than destroy on a dissolved group — is a fatal protocol error.
On creation the compositor sends the current state as one initial batch: one name event carrying the compositor-assigned group name, then one state event carrying the effective source (empty uuid when none is available) and the full mirror list, followed by one done event marking the end of the initial batch. If the create_group source was rejected, an operation_failed event is sent before the done event; for an invalid group object from get_group the batch is only an operation_failed event followed by done. Later changes are reported by further state events; the name never changes.
Several group objects may be bound to the same group, for example one from create_group and others from get_group; they all observe the same state. Destroying one object only releases that client's handle. The dissolve request tears down the group as a whole, emitting removed to every bound group object and group_removed on the manager. After removed the object is inert: only destroy is valid, and anything else is rejected with the already_dissolved error.
When a member output is unplugged or disabled the compositor updates the effective runtime state without dissolving the group: an unavailable mirror is dropped from the mirror list, and when the configured source becomes unavailable the compositor auto-promotes the first available mirror — the earliest one in the configured mirror list order — to the effective source, reporting its uuid as the source and dropping it from the mirror list in the same state event. Whether the promotion is temporary — the configured source reclaims the role when it returns — or permanent — the selected output becomes the new configured source — is a compositor implementation detail. Clients observe only the effective source and mirror list carried by each state event and must not assume either behavior. To pin a particular output as the permanent source, a client calls set_source with its uuid and then commits; if that output is currently the effective source the request succeeds idempotently.
The source uuid is empty only when the group has no available output at all: no configured source is available (or none is configured) and there is no available mirror to promote. The group itself remains. Client-driven remove_output, by contrast, removes the output from the persisted configuration.

enum.name: error
enum.description: Raised as fatal protocol errors on the group object.

entry.name: already_dissolved
entry.summary: the group has been dissolved; only destroy may be sent

enum.name: failure
enum.description: Returned by the operation_failed event when a create_group source, get_group, or a committed set_source, add_output, or remove_output request cannot be applied, or when a request is sent to an invalid group object. These reflect transient or dynamic output state (e.g. an output unplugged between the request and the commit, or already claimed by another group), not a protocol violation; the client may retry or adjust and the connection is not terminated.

entry.name: invalid_output
entry.summary: no enabled output with the provided uuid is currently connected

entry.name: duplicate_output
entry.summary: the output is already a member of this group

entry.name: output_in_use
entry.summary: the output is the source or a mirror of another group

entry.name: not_in_group
entry.summary: the output is not a member of this group

entry.name: invalid_name
entry.summary: the group object is invalid because get_group was given an empty or unknown name

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy this group object and release the client's handle. The group itself is not affected: copy mode continues, other handles remain valid, and the compositor does not emit group_removed. Use dissolve to tear down the group as a whole. It is safe to destroy an object that has already received the removed event.

request.name: set_source
request.description:
Queue the output identified by the given uuid as the configured source of the group, replacing any current configured source. The change takes effect only when the client sends commit. The previous configured source, if any, becomes a mirror: it is appended to the end of the mirror list, and when its output is available it keeps participating in copy mode as an effective mirror.
If the request cannot be applied at commit time, the compositor emits an operation_failed event and leaves the pending change unapplied: invalid_output if the uuid does not identify a connected enabled output, duplicate_output if the output is already in this group and is not the current effective source (to make a current mirror the configured source, remove it first with remove_output and then call set_source), or output_in_use if the output belongs to another group.
If the output is already the current effective source, the request succeeds idempotently: the output becomes the configured source, any previous configured source becomes a mirror. This lets a client pin an auto-promoted mirror as the permanent source.
A later set_source replaces an earlier uncommitted one; the compositor applies only the most recent source designation on commit.

arg.name: uuid
arg.summary: uuid of the output to designate as the source

request.name: add_output
request.description:
Queue the output identified by the given uuid to be appended to the end of the group's mirror list at commit time.
If the request cannot be applied at commit time, the compositor emits an operation_failed event and leaves the pending addition unapplied: invalid_output if the uuid does not identify a connected enabled output, duplicate_output if the output is already in this group, or output_in_use if it belongs to another group.

arg.name: uuid
arg.summary: uuid of the output to add as a mirror

request.name: remove_output
request.description:
Queue the removal of the output identified by the given uuid from the configured membership of the group at commit time. If the output is not a configured member at commit time, the compositor emits an operation_failed event with not_in_group and the removal is unapplied; this covers an output that was never added as well as one whose configuration was already removed.
If the removed output is the configured source or a configured mirror, the compositor re-resolves the effective source and mirror list as described in the interface description and reports the result in a state event.

arg.name: uuid
arg.summary: uuid of the member output to remove

request.name: commit
request.description:
Apply all pending set_source, add_output, and remove_output requests in the order they were queued. Requests that cannot be applied are skipped, each reported by an operation_failed event, and the remaining requests are still applied. The queue is then cleared. If any applied change altered the effective source or mirror list, the compositor emits one state event carrying the resulting effective state; otherwise no state event is emitted.
Sending commit with an empty queue is valid and does nothing. dissolve discards the pending queue.

request.name: dissolve

description.summary: dissolve the group and exit copy mode

request.description: Tear down the group: exit copy mode, remove it from the manager, and release the affected outputs. The configured source and mirror list are discarded and the group is not restored on compositor restart. The compositor emits removed to every group object bound to this group and group_removed on the manager. After removed the object is inert; only destroy is valid, and anything else — including dissolve again — is rejected with already_dissolved.

event.name: name

description.summary: the compositor-assigned name of the group

event.description: Reports the name the compositor assigned to this group. Emitted exactly once on each group object, before any other event, so the creator of the group learns its name without a group_added event. The name is unique among existing groups and never changes; a dissolved group's name may be reused by a group created later. It identifies the group in the manager's group_removed event and is the name accepted by the manager's get_group request.

arg.name: name
arg.summary: the compositor-assigned name of the group

event.name: done

description.summary: the initial state batch is complete

event.description: Emitted exactly once on each group object, immediately after the initial name and state events — or, for an invalid group object, after the operation_failed event — marking the end of the initial state batch. A client receiving this event knows it has the complete initial state of the group and that any later state event reflects a change. It is sent even when the initial source is empty and the mirror list is empty.

event.name: state

description.summary: current effective source and mirror list of the group

event.description:
Reports the current effective runtime state of the group in a single atomic event: the effective source uuid and the complete ordered list of effective mirror uuids. The client replaces any previously known state with the contents of this event; the source and the mirror list are always consistent within one emission.
The effective source is the configured source if it is currently connected and enabled; otherwise it is an auto-promoted mirror or empty, as described in the interface description. The mirror list holds the configured mirrors that are currently connected and enabled, in list order; the source output, if any, is not part of the list, and a count of zero means the group has no effective mirrors.
Emitted once on creation and again whenever the effective source or the effective mirror list changes: after a successful commit, and when any member output is unplugged, disabled, re-enabled, or replugged.
The uuids argument contains the concatenation of count uuids, one per mirror, in list order. Output uuids assigned through treeland-output-uuid-unstable-v1 are fixed-length and never contain the NUL byte; the compositor must preserve this property for every uuid it assigns, and clients may rely on it to split the array. Each uuid is therefore the array size in bytes divided by count, and parsing needs no separators: the client reads count fixed-length uuids back to back. The count argument always matches the number of uuids in the array; a client may use it to validate the array size. The list order follows the order in which mirrors were added; unavailable mirrors are filtered out without shifting the relative order of the others.

arg.name: source
arg.summary: uuid of the current effective source output, or empty when none is available

arg.name: count
arg.summary: number of mirror outputs in the list

arg.name: uuids
arg.summary: concatenation of count same-length mirror output uuids, in list order

event.name: removed
event.description: Emitted to every group object bound to the group when the group is dissolved. After this event the object is inert and the client must destroy it.

event.name: operation_failed

description.summary: a queued or requested change could not be applied

event.description: Emitted when a create_group source, get_group, or a committed set_source, add_output, or remove_output request cannot be applied, or when a request is sent to an invalid group object. For a committed set_source, add_output, or remove_output request the cause is a transient or dynamic output state, such as an output being unplugged between the request and the commit or already claimed by another group; that change is skipped and the client may retry. For a failed create_group source the group is created with an empty source and the event is emitted on the new group object before its done event. For an invalid get_group the object is invalid, no name event is sent, and every later request except destroy is rejected with invalid_name. This is not a protocol error and the connection is not terminated.

arg.name: uuid
arg.summary: the output uuid the client passed to the failing request, or empty when the failure is not about an output
